correctness.rationale: Four-point rigidity follows by the dimension-one L2 quadratic residual and rank-one determinant polynomial, forcing two antipodal lines and isotropic orthogonal axes. Exact GKW operator eigenvalues give 1/[8p(1-p)]. Trace-free Frobenius Parseval yields universal 1/4 and regular polygons attain it. For five atoms, exact equality forces a unitary five-by-five weighted Fourier matrix and regular pentagon. For Lambda <= 1/4+epsilon <= 1/4+1e-8, fourth-moment control gives radial L2 error <=4epsilon and low Fourier harmonics <=7sqrt(epsilon); spectral near-unitarity gives weights >=0.19 and <=6sqrt(epsilon) from 1/5, geometric-root separation gives angles <=300sqrt(epsilon), and radial atomwise control yields distance <=440sqrt(epsilon). The standalone checker passed 3762 finite arithmetic/numerical assertions, not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 article poses the support-size versus quadratic defect problem and gives only a support-unrestricted bound/design characterization. Classical cubature theory already covers some qualitative four-point features. The resulting exact support frontier is combined with a quantitative five-point spectral-defect inverse theorem, whose explicit uniform atomwise O(sqrt epsilon) bounds and nonconstant-radius treatment were not found in inspected same-object primary literature or targeted records. This is a qualified self-review, not independent priority certification.
residual_risks: Classical degree-three minimal cubature classifications include central symmetry; no independent originality is ascribed to this known ingredient.
An unlocated general stability theorem for positive weighted circular cubature or near-unitary Vandermonde systems might specialize to the quantitative result.
The motivating manuscript cites an unpublished companion on lattice quadratic replication; no public complete text was located, and its scope is not treated as excluded.
Searches and source inspection support a qualified novelty judgment, not absolute priority or independent validation.

value.rationale: Finite-state cardinality is a real implementation cost for moment-matched Brownian increments and the quadratic orthogonal martingale. The complete four-to-five frontier determines the exact one-extra-state effect on the best worst-direction residual, while the five-state quantitative inverse theorem forces robustness of each individual state and weight under a small spectral error. This addresses a motivated design gap and is not merely a restatement of the prior unrestricted bound or a numerical table.
